changelog: First public release of fx-fishing — Fishing & Scuba Diving System (QBCore / Qbox / ESX).
Hourly dynamic market: price multipliers now change on the hour (xx:00) and are deterministic — a server restart no longer resets prices and every player sees the same price.
Treasure (diving) prices are now connected to the same market engine on their own independent curve (Config.Diving.Market).
New countdown banner above the market panels: server time, next update time, time left and an hourly progress line (highlighted during the last 5 minutes).
Open panels refresh themselves on the hourly tick, including the sell-tab estimates.
Market exclusions are now configurable via Config.Career.Market.exclude instead of being hard-coded; the old 5-minute random-walk behaviour is still available with mode = "interval".
New NUI catch minigame system replacing the ox_lib skill check — 4 types ship in the UI: timing (sweep bar), tension (hold-to-reel with inertia), sequence (W/A/S/D series) and reel (spinning ring).
Minigame type is chosen by the server owner via Config.Minigame.Type, with an optional random mode (Config.Minigame.Random) and per-species overrides (Config.Minigame.PerFish).

Difficulty presets (easy / medium / hard / expert) are read from each species' existing skillCheck entry and can be fine-tuned per minigame type via Config.Minigame.PerType — tension gets its own softer curve.
Catch quality (0-1) is validated server-side and scales the reward: up to +25% XP and a weight roll biased toward the species' upper band (Config.Minigame.QualityBonus).
Safety timeout added: if the NUI sends no result within Config.Minigame.TimeoutMs, the fish escapes.
The legacy ox_lib skillCheck is still available with Config.Minigame.enabled = false.
Removed the illegal-fishing "caught" penalty entirely: no more automatic item seizure and no player-facing "caught" notification.

The heat/suspicion system and its HUD bar are unchanged; crossing the catch-chance threshold now only sends a dispatch alert to police, who handle the rest via roleplay (they can already search the player's inventory).
Removed the now-unused Config.Illegal.seizePercentOnCaught setting and the illegal_caught_feeling locale string.

SECURITY/EXPLOIT FIX: a crew dive multiplied the crate count by the crew size at mission start, but nothing ever checked whether the crew actually dived. A player could invite members, leave them standing at the shop, dive alone and loot every extra crate plus the crew XP bonus by himself.

Crew crates are now gated live: at any moment only site.crateCount x (members currently diving inside the mission area) crates can be opened. The rest stay locked until the crew shows up. The check runs on every crate search, so members who leave mid-dive re-lock the remaining crates.
The crew XP multiplier now follows the number of members actually present at the site instead of the roster size.

New Config.Diving.Team.Presence block tunes the check: area tolerance (radiusPad), whether being underwater is required, and a grace period (graceSec, default 120s) so tank swaps, deaths and short trips to the surface never lock a legitimate crew out. Set enabled = false to restore the old behaviour.

Solo and crew dives are now separate. The Dive Sites tab ALWAYS starts a solo mission: no crate multiplier, no XP bonus, and only your own zone cooldown is spent. Crew missions are started from the My Crew tab. Previously any dive started while in a crew of 2 or more silently became a crew mission and burnt every member's zone cooldown.
Crew members without manage rights can now start their own solo dive from the Dive Sites tab; they used to be rejected with a no-permission error.
Starting a dive while another mission is already active now shows a clear message instead of reporting your own name as being busy elsewhere.

ox_inventory FIX - using a fishing rod did nothing on some ox_inventory servers. ox only runs a use handler for items that declare one; without it the item is silently ignored. The 5 rods and diving_suit in setup/items/ox_inventory.lua now ship with client = { event = 'fx-fishing:client:oxUseItem' }. ACTION REQUIRED: ox_inventory servers must re-paste those 6 item definitions into ox_inventory/data/items.lua. Note this is 'event', not 'export' - an export would also set consume = 1 and delete the rod on first use.

The client bridge now accepts three use paths (ox client.event, ox_inventory:usedItem as a fallback, and the qb/qbx/esx usable item) with a 750 ms debounce, so no setup can trigger a cast twice. diving_suit is routed through the same point, which also fixes the suit being equipped and unequipped in one click on ox.

PANEL FIX - the career panel opened empty for some players, showing raw locale keys (nav_market, GUIDE_RODS, page_market_sub) and empty shop lists. The NUI init message was sent on a fixed 500 ms timer and was lost whenever the browser had not finished loading, which only happened on slower machines or busy servers. The UI now announces itself with a uiReady callback and the data is sent on demand, re-sent if the ping is missed, and re-checked every time the panel opens.

CRASH FIX - a missing command name in the config made RegisterCommand throw 'native 0x5FA79B0F: Argument at index 0 was null', which killed the rest of that client file (the diving system in particular). Command registration is now nil-safe: an empty name is skipped with a console warning, and setting a command key to false disables it silently on purpose.

Framework and inventory auto-detection no longer depend on the server.cfg order. A resource that is still 'starting' is now recognised, and detection is retried for 20 seconds. Previously, starting fx-fishing before ox_inventory made every item operation silently fail.

Notifications are never dropped any more: if no framework is detected, or it arrives late, the message falls back to ox_lib instead of disappearing. A failed server callback now reports that the server did not respond instead of leaving the player with no feedback.

New diagnostics - 'fxfishdiag' (server console) prints the detected framework, inventory and the state of every related resource; '/fxfishdebug' (F8) checks every item against ox_inventory and reports whether client.event is wired; '/fxfishtest' (F8) bypasses the inventory and starts a cast directly, which separates an item-definition problem from a server-side one. On ox, missing item definitions are also listed in red on start.
Config.Debug now logs the full item-use to cast flow in F8. Setup documentation was updated with the ox_inventory use-handler requirement and a diagnosis walkthrough.
